predecessors.name: Irish Free State
predecessors.text: the twenty-six counties of the Irish Free State, unchanged by the 1937 Constitution

ledger.x: 29 December 1937: the Constitution of Ireland creates Éire.
29 December 1937: the state is born with three ports still British.
29 December 1937: the Berehaven forts are still British ('The Berehaven forts were handed over' only on 29 September 1938).
29 December 1937: the Lough Swilly forts at Dunree and Leenan are still British.
11 July 1938: Spike Island is handed back.
29 September 1938: the Berehaven forts are handed back.
3 October 1938: the Lough Swilly forts at Dunree and Leenan are surrendered to Irish forces, the last of the Treaty Ports; the Agreement had set 31 December 1938 as the latest date.
18 April 1949: the state becomes the Republic of Ireland.

certainty.note: The state is the twenty-six counties and shares its only land border with Northern Ireland; the Constitution's claim to the whole island (Articles 2 and 3, 1937) was removed in 1999 and never moved the border.
